newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: MONTENEGRO TO CALL TENDER FOR POWER PLANTS - PAPER.
newsitem.headline: MONTENEGRO TO CALL TENDER FOR POWER PLANTS - PAPER.

text.p: Montenegro has called an international tender for building a hydroelectric power plant system on the Moraca river, Belgrade daily Nasa Borba reported on Monday.

"The tender concerns four hydroelectric power plants which should utilise natural water resources of the Moraca river," Miodrag Gomilanovic, the republic's Minister for Industry, Mining and Energy, was quoted by the paper as saying.

"Besides the tender to be published in the Yugoslav Official Gazette, direct offers have been sent to the countries that have earlier showed interest for plants' construction," he added, giving no other details.
Belgrade-based construction, engineering and design company Energoprojekt has prepared the documentation for the international tender, the report said.

Montenegro, Serbia's junior partner in the Yugoslav federation, has warned of chronic power shortages and said its power industry could not produce enough to meet domestic needs nor did it have money for imports.
"Montenegro will face 700-800 million KWh shortage of electricity this year," Gomilanovic said.
He said the republic's power industry has not produced one single KWh in August.
Piva, the largest Montenegro's hydroelectric power plant, does not operate since Serbia's power company decided to preserve Piva lake water levels.
Montenegro's and Serbia's power companies have a cooperation deal on production and distribution of electricity.

The Perucica hydroelectric power plant was under overhaul, and the Plevlja thermal electric power plant was not yet ready for connection to the grid after two and a half months reconstruction, Gomilanovic said.
